categories.name: False Urgency
categories.description: Pressure to act or share immediately, before the reader can think or verify.

categories.name: Fake Authority
categories.description: Borrowed or invented credibility — vague experts, misused titles, unnamed insiders.

categories.name: Emotional Bait
categories.description: Content designed to trigger a strong emotional reaction before critical thinking kicks in.

categories.name: Fake Consensus
categories.description: Implying everyone already believes or knows this, pressuring agreement through perceived popularity.

categories.name: Cherry-Picked / Misleading Statistics
categories.description: Real-sounding numbers presented without context, baseline, or source.

categories.name: AI-Generated Content Cues
categories.description: Subtle tells that an image, video, voice clip, or piece of text may be AI-generated or manipulated.

posts.text: ⚠️ Ye message 2 ghante mein delete ho jayega. Abhi 10 logo ko forward karo warna important update miss ho jayega.
posts.explanation: Fake countdown pressure removes the time needed to pause and verify — urgency is designed to make you act before you think, not because any real deadline exists.

posts.text: URGENT: Your bank account will be frozen in 30 minutes unless you verify your details at this link right now.
posts.explanation: Combines a fake deadline with a threat to something the reader cares about (their money) — a structure behind the vishing/smishing scam pattern that has grown sharply worldwide.

posts.text: Sarkar ne ye khabar 1 ghante mein hataa di jayegi. Screenshot lelo abhi, baad mein nahi milegi.
posts.explanation: Claims of imminent censorship make content feel rare and important, encouraging quick sharing before anyone checks whether it's true.

posts.text: Limited slots left — offer expires in 09:59. Claim now before it's gone forever.
posts.explanation: Countdown timers exploit loss aversion, a well-documented psychological trigger that pressures snap decisions over careful evaluation.

posts.text: Bank ne bola hai KYC abhi update nahi kiya to account 24 ghante mein band ho jayega. Neeche diye link pe click karke turant verify karo.
posts.explanation: Mirrors one of the most common real fraud patterns in India today — fake urgency plus a fake bank threat, designed to trigger immediate action over verification.

posts.text: Ek senior doctor ne bataya — haldi wala doodh cancer tak theek kar sakta hai. Hospital wale nahi batate kyunki business band ho jayega.
posts.explanation: "A senior doctor" is unnamed and unverifiable, borrowing the credibility of a medical title without any accountability.

posts.text: A former Big Tech insider confirms: this app is secretly recording everything you say. Leaked internal memo proves it.
posts.explanation: "Former insider" and "leaked memo" imply exclusive, verified access, but name no person, document, or company — vague authority used to feel credible without being checkable.

posts.text: IIT ke scientists ne prove kar diya hai — ye ek cheez khane se sugar completely control ho jaata hai, medicine ki zaroorat nahi.
posts.explanation: Naming a prestigious institution generically (no specific researcher, paper, or study cited) borrows credibility without providing anything a reader could verify.

posts.text: As someone who used to work in finance, trust me — this investment app guarantees 40% returns every month with zero risk.
posts.explanation: A vague professional background implies insider knowledge, while the claim itself (guaranteed 40% monthly, zero risk) contradicts how real investments work.

posts.text: Mera rishtedaar ISRO mein kaam karta hai, usne bataya ki ye news sach hai but officially release nahi hui hai.
posts.explanation: Unverifiable second-hand "insider" claims feel credible because they're framed as secret — but there's no way to confirm the relative, the job, or the claim.

posts.text: Is bacchi ko ilaj nahi mil paya kyunki naye rules aa gaye hain. Agar dil hai to share karo.
posts.explanation: Emotionally charged imagery paired with a moral challenge pressures sharing based on feeling, not on whether the underlying claim is accurate.

posts.text: You won't believe what this company just did to its employees. Every worker deserves to see this.
posts.explanation: Vague outrage-bait creates anger before any actual facts are presented, so the reader is emotionally invested before evaluating the claim.

posts.text: Agar ye video nahi rulaya to samajh lena dil pathar ka hai. Please sabko bhejo.
posts.explanation: Explicitly weaponizing tears/emotion as "proof" the content deserves to be shared substitutes emotional reaction for evidence.

posts.text: This should make every parent furious. Share before they take this down too.
posts.explanation: Combines anger-bait with a suggestion of suppression, making content feel urgent and important without offering anything independently verifiable.

posts.text: Meri dadi ko isi tarah ka call aaya tha, awaaz bilkul mere cousin jaisi thi — agar aisa call aaye to turant paise mat bhejo.
posts.explanation: Mirrors the real, rapidly growing global 'grandparent scam' pattern using voice-cloning. Here emotional framing is used protectively — a good discussion point that the technique itself isn't inherently bad, just the intent behind it.

posts.text: 10 lakh se zyada logo ne ye already share kar diya hai. Aap abhi tak unaware ho?
posts.explanation: Large, unverifiable numbers create social pressure — if "everyone" already believes it, questioning it starts to feel socially risky.

posts.text: Everyone in my friend group is switching to this — why isn't this all over the mainstream news?
posts.explanation: Implies both popular agreement and suppressed truth at once, making skepticism feel naive rather than sensible.

posts.text: Poore mohalle mein log yahi bol rahe hain. Itne log galat kaise ho sakte hain?
posts.explanation: Popularity within a trusted local group is used as a stand-in for accuracy — but something widely repeated says nothing about whether it's true.

posts.text: Join the millions who already know the truth. Don't be the last one to find out.
posts.explanation: Frames the decision socially rather than factually, pressuring conformity instead of verification.

posts.text: Family group ke sabhi log ye maan rahe hain, tum akele hi doubt kyun kar rahe ho?
posts.explanation: Social pressure from a trusted in-group (family) discourages disagreement, making healthy skepticism feel like a betrayal of relationships.

posts.text: Cases up 90% this month! (the real number went from 2 to just under 4)
posts.explanation: A large percentage sounds alarming, but without the actual counts, it's impossible to judge whether the change is meaningful.

posts.text: Is scheme se 300% zyada fraud ho raha hai! (original number kabhi nahi bataya gaya)
posts.explanation: Relative change sounds dramatic, but without the starting figure, there's no way to judge real-world scale — technically accurate numbers used to mislead.

posts.text: 9 out of 10 people we asked prefer this (based on a poll of 10 people in one office).
posts.explanation: A statistically meaningless sample size is dressed up as a general truth — technically accurate, wildly unrepresentative.

posts.text: Naye rule ke baad business 50% girr gaya (sales already gir rahi thi unrelated reasons se, months pehle se).
posts.explanation: A real number is presented without the context needed to judge whether the new rule actually caused the change — correlation framed as causation.

posts.text: Only 2% of people know this one fact (no named source, survey, or method given).
posts.explanation: A precise-sounding number implies real data behind it, but without a citation, the figure could be entirely invented.

posts.text: Image of a crowd at an event — hands have an extra finger, background signage text is garbled, shadows fall in different directions across the same scene.
posts.explanation: Current AI image generators still struggle with fine details like hands, readable background text, and physically consistent lighting.

posts.text: Voice note, supposedly from a family member — tone is unusually flat and consistent throughout, no breathing sounds, background is unnaturally silent for a phone call.
posts.explanation: Maps to the real grandparent-scam pattern law enforcement is tracking closely. AI-generated speech often sounds 'too clean', lacking natural breathing and ambient noise. A pre-agreed family safe phrase is a strong defense since no AI can generate something it hasn't heard.

posts.text: Text post with generic phrasing that repeats the same idea in slightly different words, no specific names, dates, or checkable details anywhere.
posts.explanation: AI-generated text often 'pads' length without adding new information and avoids concrete, verifiable specifics.

posts.text: Video clip of a company executive announcing a 'guaranteed' investment — mouth movements slightly out of sync with audio, unnaturally smooth skin texture, mechanical blinking pattern.
posts.explanation: Lip-sync drift and over-smoothed skin remain common deepfake artifacts — and deepfaked executives promoting bogus investments is a documented real fraud pattern.

posts.text: Image where reflections in a mirror or window don't match what's actually in the room; the same light source produces shadows falling in inconsistent directions.
posts.explanation: AI image generators frequently get physically impossible details wrong. Mismatched reflections and inconsistent shadows are strong tells no real photograph would produce.
